name: Solomon
bio:
Solomon was a son born to David in Jerusalem, first named simply among his many brothers (2 Samuel 5:14) — the child who would grow up to inherit David's throne, build the temple the LORD promised through Nathan, and become Israel's most celebrated king for his wisdom and wealth.

Solomon's birth is told in full after David's affair with Bathsheba and the death of their first child, born while Uriah was still her husband. After that infant's death, David comforted Bathsheba, and she conceived again; the son she bore was named Solomon, and the LORD loved him, sending word through the prophet Nathan that he should also be called Jedidiah, meaning "beloved of the LORD" (2 Samuel 12:24-25) — a quiet sign of grace at the start of a story shadowed by his parents' sin. As David grew old, his son Adonijah tried to seize the throne for himself, but Nathan and Bathsheba moved David to honor his earlier oath that Solomon would reign; David had Solomon anointed king at Gihon by Zadok and Nathan while he himself still lived, ensuring a peaceful transfer of power (1 Kings 1). Before he died, David charged Solomon to walk faithfully in the LORD's ways and to deal wisely with the unfinished business of his reign — bringing Joab to account for his bloodshed, showing continued kindness to Barzillai's family, and settling accounts with Shimei (1 Kings 2:1-9). Solomon's kingdom was established once David died, but Adonijah's request to marry Abishag, David's former attendant, struck Solomon as a renewed bid for the throne; he had Adonijah executed, exiled Abiathar from the priesthood, had Benaiah strike down Joab at the altar where he had fled for sanctuary, and ultimately had Shimei put to death for breaking the terms of his pardon — securing the kingdom firmly in his own hands (1 Kings 2:10-46).

His rise to the throne, his reign, and his legacy unfold in detail across the rest of Samuel, 1 Kings, and 1-2 Chronicles.
